title: Tailgating through the side door
brief: 18:10. You are badging back in at the staff side door. A courier with an armful of boxes asks you to hold it.
insight: Holding a door is good manners everywhere except a secure door. That is exactly what tailgating relies on.
teaches: Let the door close behind you: everyone badges in on their own
Say no politely and point to the right way in, without arguing
Hand an unexpected visitor to security rather than deciding alone

card.title: “Cheers, can you hold that?”
card.imageAlt: A courier in a hi vis vest holding a stack of parcels
body: 18:10. You nipped out to the car park and you are badging back in at the side door, the staff only one.
A courier in a hi vis vest, arms full of boxes, jogs up behind you. “Cheers, can you hold that? Delivery for finance, my hands are full.”
No delivery is booked tonight, and reception closed at six.

choices.label: Hold the door, their hands are full
“Sorry, I cannot let you in this way. Security can help you at the front.”
“Have you got a visitor badge or a booking?”
A courier tried to follow me in the side door

script.say: Thanks for not letting them in. Nothing is booked tonight. I will check the camera and meet them outside.

setup.title: Side door
setup.body: You are heading back in from the car park

door.objective: Get back in through the side door.
door.insight: “My hands are full” is a script. It works because refusing feels rude.

hint.text: Pick up your badge to head back in. Do not hold the door for someone who has not badged.

outcome.label: Held the door for the courier
outcome.what: An unknown person is now inside, after hours, heading for the finance floor, and the badge system says nobody came in.
outcome.ideal: lets a secure door close behind them, however full someone's hands are.

card.title: A stranger on the finance floor
body: You held the door and the courier walked in behind you. The badge log shows only you. The boxes were empty.
A few minutes on an empty floor is enough to plug a device into a spare port or photograph a desk. The polite answer was the right one: “Sorry, you will need to go round the front.”
card.ideal: lets the door close and sends visitors to the right entrance.

outcome.label: Said no, politely
outcome.what: Polite, firm, and pointing to the right way in. Nobody needs to argue at a door.
outcome.ideal: refuses a tailgate politely and points to the proper entrance.

outcome.label: Asked for a badge or a booking
outcome.what: A fair question, but anyone can say yes. The door still should not be held.
outcome.ideal: does not let the answer to a question open a secure door.

push.objective: The courier is not giving up.

auto.title: “Come on, two seconds”
auto.imageAlt: The courier, still holding the parcels
body: “Come on, I am here every day. Two seconds, I will leave it on the first desk. If this goes back I will get the blame.”
The door is closing behind you.

choices.label: “Sorry, I really cannot. Security will sort it for you.” Let it close.

hint.text: Stay polite and let the door close.

outcome.label: Held firm under pressure
outcome.what: Guilt and urgency are the tools. You did not have to win the argument, only let the door close.
outcome.ideal: stays polite and firm when pushed.

outcome.label: Gave in and let them through
outcome.what: The courier is inside. Pushing a little harder was all it took.
outcome.ideal: does not let pressure open a secure door.

card.title: Pressure opened the door
body: The second push worked. The guilt, the rush and “two seconds” are the script. Nobody gets the blame for a door closing.
Security was one phone call away and deals with deliveries every night.
card.ideal: lets the door close and passes the visitor to security.

report.objective: Back at your desk: let security know.

hint.text: Call security on 4999 from the desk phone, or raise a Helpdesk ticket (someone trying to get into the building).

outcome.label: Told security
outcome.what: Mo checks the camera and deals with the courier. That is the job of security, not yours.
outcome.ideal: reports a tailgating attempt so security can act.

outcome.label: Logged it
outcome.what: There is a record of the attempt at the side door.
